green lion.modern: A volatile, corrosive intermediate — often associated with antimony regulus preparations or acidic distillates in Newton's notebooks
green lion.notes: One of the most famous alchemical cover names. Newton encountered it in Philalethes and other sources.

star regulus.modern: Crystalline antimony regulus (Sb) with radiating star-like facets, produced by reducing antimony ore with iron
star regulus.notes: Newton repeated this process many times, varying the iron and fusion duration. Central to his chymical investigations.

sophic mercury.modern: A purified, 'philosophical' mercury — not common quicksilver alone, but a prepared mercurial substance central to many recipes
sophic mercury.notes: Newton distinguished common ☿ from 'sophic' or 'animated' mercury in transcriptions.

spirit of salt.modern: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) or its vapors, produced by distilling salt with vitriol
spirit of salt.notes: Newton produced and used mineral acids extensively in displacement and dissolution experiments.

tree of diana.modern: Crystalline silver arborescences from silver-mercury amalgam in solution
tree of diana.notes: A striking 'vegetative' metal growth. Newman and Reck have replicated this in modern labs.

philosopher's stone.modern: The hypothetical agent of transmutation and perfection — Newton sought understanding of affinities, not literal gold-making alone
philosopher's stone.notes: Newton's private goal was deeper matter theory, not mere coinage.

antimony.modern: Elemental antimony (Sb), symbol ♁ in Newton's notebooks
antimony.notes: Key to the Star Regulus experiments and many fusion trials.
